opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor Engineer. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; no training info on record from HR. Recommend read for Payroll access.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB confirms E045 is a contractor with basic security training (not advanced). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds maximum; recommend read for Payroll.
reason: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor Engineer with basic security training (not advanced). Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. Since requested write exceeds the maximum allowed (read), the maximum of read is granted for Payroll.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Douglas Salinas (E045)
Requested: write access to Payroll
Role: Engineer
Employment type: contractor
Security training: basic (not advanced)

Policy for contractors: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Since the employee is a contractor with basic (not advanced) training, the maximum access is read. Requested write is above the maximum, so grant the maximum = read.

Both HR and Security recommend read. So decision: read.
